I am 76 years old and have farmed these fields in Quzhou for over fifty years. I do not see any reason to change what has always worked. The land I still manage myself is 6 mu — less than when I was young, but enough for me and my family. I will plant winter wheat this October and follow it with summer maize after the wheat harvest in early June. This wheat-maize rotation is what every household around here does; the machinery, the seed dealers, and the buyers all expect it.

For wheat, I will rotary-till the soil before sowing, because that is easier on my back than deep ploughing and gives a fine seedbed. I will sow about 30 jin of improved seed per mu — probably *Jimai 22* or *Luyuan 502*, the same varieties my neighbors use. I will spread a basal compound fertilizer of roughly 100 kg per mu, something like 18-22-5, and topdress once in spring with urea or a compound mix. That comes to about 20 kg of nitrogen, 22 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium per mu. I will irrigate four times: the winter irrigation, the jointing water, the heading water, and one grouting water. I will spray twice for insects, once for weeds, and once for fungus — about four pesticide applications in total. I expect around 1,000 kg per mu if the spring rains cooperate.

For summer maize, I will no-till plant right after the wheat harvest in mid-June. There is no time to waste — the heat units are tight. I will use one package per mu of hybrid seed, most likely *Denghai 605*, because it is drought-tolerant and yields well. I will apply basal compound fertilizer at about 80 kg per mu, giving roughly 24 kg nitrogen, 7 kg phosphorus, and 7 kg potassium per mu. Maize needs less irrigation than wheat here; two good irrigations, one at the jointing stage and one at the grain-filling stage, are usually enough. I will spray twice for corn borers and armyworms and once for weeds — three pesticide rounds. I expect about 1,150 kg per mu.

I keep my inputs moderate. I am not a family farm with new equipment, and I do not chase the highest possible yield with extra fertilizer anymore. I know these numbers by heart, and they give me a stable harvest without emptying my pockets or wearing me out.
